name: Tehachapi Mountains

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: River deposits are a mix of gravel, sand and silt. They are often fertile, so vines can grow vigorously.
soil.top: The topsoil drains fast and warms early in spring. Vines get little water, which keeps crops small and flavors concentrated, but drought bites hard. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
